correctness.rationale: The proof starts from both left and right increasing-length Demazure multiplication, shows that a central permutation either fixes each adjacent pair or has that index simultaneously a left and right descent, peels outer endpoints by a necessary-and-sufficient induction, and proves that multiplication by the outer transposition advances one nested reversal until the longest element absorbs. Thus every n >= 2 and every product are covered. A separately constructed reduced-word checker enumerated all permutations through n=8 and verified every central product. Finite checks supplement the complete proof.

evidence: Berenstein, Greenstein and Li, arXiv:2605.09761, §3.3 establishes commuting pairs of idempotents; §4.18 and Corollary 4.20 give explicit products of parabolic elements, including the nested-reversal candidates. The earlier theorem already covers the multiplication law among such known parabolic elements, a portion explicitly credited here.
Published Catalan maximal-clique type-A result studies only monoid idempotents and expressly does not classify nonidempotent commutative submonoids.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The strongest close published findings imply or explain the product formula for candidate elements but do not assert that these, and only these, commute with *every* generator. This remaining center-membership characterization is the independent contribution. No claim of originality is made for prior parabolic multiplication.

originality.rationale: The complete classification of individual monoid-central elements via an iff generator test was not found in the inspected published literature or own accessible claim history. Closest König linear-algebra center is a different object; Berenstein-Greenstein-Li covers the product formula among already identified parabolic elements and commuting idempotents, while the closest public type-A work covers idempotents only. Novelty is limited to the exhaustive center classification, not the established parabolic-product relations; historical priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: An explicit or implicit older monoid-center classification may exist within broad Coxeter/Hecke monoid folklore not captured by semantic searches.
The known general parabolic product laws imply the multiplicative structure of the proposed center after its elements are identified; that component is not claimed as independently novel.
The general algebra-center basis could in principle be specialized by further coefficient arguments; this is not identical to a published explicit classification of the monoid center.

value.rationale: The center of a standard finite Coxeter monoid is a natural, structurally motivated invariant. The theorem completely identifies it for every degree, exhibits a growing chain of central nonidempotent powers with a sharp absorbing exponent, and separates monoid-centrality from algebra-center linear combinations. This is a full infinite-family semigroup classification rather than a textbook substitution or arbitrary small case.
